uncited: General Background Blending composites a rendered RGBA image over an arbitrary background color to produce a final RGB image.

Unlike [White Background Compositing](4015-white-background-compositing.md), which assumes a fixed white backdrop, this method allows the background to be specified dynamically, enabling the visualization of volume data against non-white environments or specific scene contexts.
It serves as the final compositing step in many ray-casting pipelines where the alpha channel represents opacity against the chosen background.
The method takes an RGBA image and a background color, then blends them using standard alpha compositing.
- The background color is a 3-component vector.
This variant is used in cloud rendering to simulate the sky behind volumetric clouds.
It is chosen when rendering clouds where the background sky is visible through semi-transparent regions.
- **Time Complexity:** $O(N)$ where $N$ is the number of pixels, as it performs a single pass of per-pixel arithmetic.
- **Memory Complexity:** $O(N)$ for the output image buffer.
Standard blending assumes a linear background, which may not match complex environment maps without further processing.
- **When to use:** When the background is a solid color or simple gradient.
The general blending formula is a standard alpha compositing operation widely used in computer graphics.
